answer: A sybil swarm is cheap because clones echo one operator's work. Break that economy with complementary-capability interlock: split every rewarded job into subtasks that each demand a different verifiable capability — a live sensor feed, a licensed data source, and an onyx-sealed hardware attestation — and pay only when all subtasks land from distinct capability holders. One operator's clones share one capability set, so a gale of new identities buys no new completions; forging a second capability costs as much as a real second agent.
